video_title: Why Did 67 Companies Opt Out of Tokenized Stock Trading on OKX ICE?
gist: Laura Shin hosts Securitize president Brett Redford and SEC Trading & Markets director Jamie Selway on why 67 companies opted out of tokenized trading on OKX ICE's tokenized securities venue (TSV) under the SEC's 5-year innovation exemption: rushed notices and anti-tokenization campaigns (with alleged Nasdaq involvement) drove knee-jerk opt-outs, while the SEC defends issuer consent, no synthetics, volume caps, and targets a 2027 rule proposal; Securitize contrasts its broker-dealer/issuer-sponsored model now at 47 names.

themes.theme: OKX ICE opt-outs and issuer pushback

insights.claim: 67 companies notified by OKX ICE have opted out of having their stock tokenized on its TSV, leaving the launch dominated by crypto-related names such as Strategy, Coinbase, Circle and Robinhood plus 59 ETFs (70+ assets), launching November 23.
insights.speaker: Laura Shin (host)
insights.so_what: Early onshore tokenized-equity liquidity will concentrate in crypto-adjacent equities and ETFs, not mega-cap tech.

insights.claim: Brett Redford says many issuers opted out reflexively because TSV notices went out before issuers were educated, and law firms warned that missing the 30-day window would lock them in for 5 years.
insights.speaker: Brett Redford (Securitize)
insights.so_what: Opt-outs reflect process friction rather than settled hostility; opt-in rates could rise as education improves.
insights.quote: I think the opt out was sort of the easiest short-term solution

insights.claim: Issuer consent is TSV-by-TSV and issuers can opt in later; OKX ICE voluntarily lets issuers opt out even after the 30-day period, going beyond the SEC's minimum rules.
insights.speaker: Jamie Selway (SEC)
insights.so_what: Reversible participation lowers the cost for issuers to experiment; watch for later opt-ins.

insights.claim: Selway says the SEC had no target opt-in rate - zero opt-ins would have been bad and 70 for 70 excessive - and calls it very early with the exemption only about two months old.
insights.speaker: Jamie Selway (SEC)
insights.so_what: Regulator is not treating the opt-outs as a failure signal.
insights.quote: I guess zero uh opt-ins would have been bad uh and probably going 70 for 70 would have been excessive.

insights.claim: Selway says issuer negativity stems from offshore unregulated synthetic tokens, where tokenization was 'done to them as opposed to done with them', and the onshore regime is repairing that experience.
insights.speaker: Jamie Selway (SEC)
insights.so_what: Offshore synthetics (e.g., Robinhood's tokenized AMC spat) poisoned issuer sentiment toward all tokenization.
insights.quote: tokenization was done to them as opposed to done with them

insights.claim: A journalist reported a Nasdaq-listed company exec was contacted by their Nasdaq rep suggesting they object to OKX ICE tokenized trading; Redford frames it as exchanges protecting issuer relationships against a model that bypasses exchanges and broker-dealers.
insights.speaker: Laura Shin (host); Brett Redford
insights.so_what: Incumbent exchange competition is shaping tokenization adoption; Nasdaq is pursuing its own tokenization model.
insights.quote: for exchanges, a lot of what it's about is being close to issuers and keeping those issuers on their exchange

insights.claim: JPMorgan Chase opted out of OKX ICE but told CoinDesk it remains encouraged by tokenization and will keep evaluating opportunities.
insights.speaker: Laura Shin (host)
insights.so_what: Blue-chip opt-outs are 'not now' rather than 'never'.

insights.claim: An anonymous group, the Common Sense Leadership Fund, ran a full-page Wall Street Journal ad telling CEOs crypto would tokenize their shares on unregulated venues; Selway calls it misleading because TSVs require US persons, permissioned wallets and SEC examination, and tokens must carry all shareholder rights.
insights.speaker: Jamie Selway (SEC)
insights.so_what: Organized lobbying against TSVs exists; regulator is publicly rebutting it.
insights.quote: the notion that it's uh totally unregulated is wrong

insights.claim: Applied Optoelectronics opted out citing uncertainty about effects on stock price, liquidity and volatility; Selway says TSVs must make the market-quality case to issuers just as exchanges do in listing decisions.
insights.speaker: Jamie Selway (SEC)
insights.so_what: TSVs will compete like exchanges on liquidity and volatility metrics.

insights.claim: The SEC's innovation exemption, issued September 17, is a 5-year conditional exemption letting TSVs trade tokenized exchange-listed stocks via permissioned automated market makers without registering as exchanges or brokers.
insights.speaker: Laura Shin (host)
insights.so_what: Creates a new class of on-chain secondary venues for US equities.

insights.claim: The exemption caps each TSV at 25 basis points of volume share in the most liquid stocks and 2.5% in less liquid stocks, and the 5-year term is meant to force permanent rulemaking.
insights.speaker: Jamie Selway (SEC)
insights.so_what: Volume caps limit near-term disruption to incumbent exchanges and market makers.

insights.claim: The SEC excluded synthetics and required tokens to carry all rights of the security because the digital-asset community it consulted wanted securities entitlements, not derivatives; synthetics would also pull in security-based swap rules.
insights.speaker: Jamie Selway (SEC); Brett Redford
insights.so_what: Onshore tokenized equities will be real-share-backed; synthetic exposure stays offshore for now.

insights.claim: Selway would not rule out tokenized derivatives later, noting single-stock and 2x single-stock ETFs already offer compliant synthetic exposure, and hopes to move from exemption to rulemaking within about a year.
insights.speaker: Jamie Selway (SEC)
insights.so_what: A path for tokenized synthetic products exists if brokers request it.
insights.quote: never never is a long time

insights.claim: The exemption is silent on how tokenization happens, so it covers both issuer-sponsored and third-party tokens, which is why the SEC did not adopt the Securities Transfer Association's request to limit it to issuer-sponsored tokens.
insights.speaker: Jamie Selway (SEC)
insights.so_what: Third-party tokenizers (including DTCC's program) can feed TSVs.

insights.claim: Selway expects the SEC's TSV rule proposal to be a 2027 event, with regular FAQs issued in the meantime to fix issues like notice-period ergonomics.
insights.speaker: Jamie Selway (SEC)
insights.so_what: Regulatory timeline for permanent tokenized-trading rules.
insights.quote: that's got to be a 2027 event in terms of getting a proposal out there.

insights.claim: Selway says the SEC under Chairman Atkins prefers building onshore over tearing down offshore venues, but US investors accessing offshore synthetic tokens on unregistered exchanges is non-compliant and geofencing enforcement could follow.
insights.speaker: Jamie Selway (SEC)
insights.so_what: Enforcement risk for offshore tokenized-stock platforms leaking to US users.
insights.quote: If US investors are um are accessing you know these synthetic tokens overseas um that's not that's not compliant.

insights.claim: Redford argues tokenization adds utility rather than fixing liquid US equity markets: use in lending pools, portable collateral, peer-to-peer transfer, global access and a quicker path to 24/7 trading.
insights.speaker: Brett Redford (Securitize)
insights.so_what: Value proposition rests on collateral and DeFi composability, not cheaper execution.

insights.claim: Offshore synthetic stock tokens proved demand: many global investors are eager for US securities and buy them despite missing basic shareholder rights.
insights.speaker: Brett Redford (Securitize)
insights.so_what: Large untapped global retail demand for US equities is the growth driver for tokenization platforms.

insights.claim: Selway cites two issuer benefits: reaching wallet-only younger investors who want tokenized Nvidia beside Bitcoin, and issuer visibility into retail holders (otherwise hidden in DTCC street name) to cross-sell products.
insights.speaker: Jamie Selway (SEC)
insights.so_what: Issuer-sponsored tokenization could reintermediate companies with their shareholders - a challenge to street-name custody.

insights.claim: In issuer-sponsored tokenization, Securitize removes shares from DTCC's nominee and puts them back on the transfer agent register so the token is the security, giving issuers line of sight to investors for discounts, benefits and voting.
insights.speaker: Brett Redford (Securitize)
insights.so_what: Threat to DTCC/Cede & Co intermediation model if it scales.

insights.claim: DTCC's tokenization pilot went live, with collateral mobility over weekends a core use case that could avoid liquidity crunches like Robinhood's during the meme stock craze; DTCC plans to expand to Solana in the second half of 2027.
insights.speaker: Jamie Selway (SEC); Laura Shin
insights.so_what: Market-infrastructure incumbents are adopting tokenization for collateral efficiency.

insights.claim: Redford expects tokenized stocks to unlock stock-loan economics for holders and allow using stock as collateral for purchases, whereas today rehypothecation benefits accrue to intermediaries; Selway notes the exemption itself does not permit lending.
insights.speaker: Brett Redford; Jamie Selway
insights.so_what: Prime brokerage and securities-lending revenue could migrate on-chain over time.

insights.claim: Securitize launched 22 more tokenized stocks, reaching 47 names and aiming for 50 within a week or two, including Apple, Microsoft, Nvidia, Alphabet, Tesla, Meta, Amazon, Exxon Mobil, GameStop, Salesforce and Disney.
insights.speaker: Brett Redford (Securitize)
insights.so_what: Securitize is building the broadest onshore tokenized equity catalog outside the TSV regime.
insights.quote: so we're now up to 47 names

insights.claim: Securitize's tokenized stocks trade through its broker-dealer at or inside the NBBO with Reg NMS and best execution, via a single-dealer RFQ with partner Jump Trading's prop AMM, and will also be offered to OKX's TSV; there is no opt-out for simply tokenizing a stock outside the exemption.
insights.speaker: Brett Redford (Securitize)
insights.so_what: Two-track model lets Securitize avoid issuer opt-out risk while still supplying TSVs.

insights.claim: OKX ICE's TSV trades on X Layer while Securitize's tokens trade on Solana, with bridging between the two for overlapping stocks.
insights.speaker: Brett Redford (Securitize)
insights.so_what: Chain choice for tokenized equities is fragmenting; bridges become infrastructure.

insights.claim: The first TSV launch under the exemption, a Canton-based venue on November 4, listed only Canton Strategic Holdings, which Selway suggests was a proof of concept that Canton qualifies as a permissioned public chain for AMMs.
insights.speaker: Jamie Selway (SEC)
insights.so_what: Canton positioning itself for collateral infrastructure in tokenized markets.

insights.claim: Other entrants include NYSE using Avalanche as its tokenization backend and Formation Securities launching in early 2027 on Solana with Galaxy, Exodus and Forward Industries; the SEC lists about four TSV notice filers.
insights.speaker: Laura Shin (host); Jamie Selway
insights.so_what: Avalanche and Solana are winning tokenized-equity backend mandates.

insights.claim: Redford dismisses fragmentation concerns, noting US equities already trade across 18 exchanges going on 20, 35-40 dark pools and multiple single-dealer platforms - 60+ venues.
insights.speaker: Brett Redford (Securitize)
insights.so_what: Tokenized venues are additive competition rather than a new fragmentation problem.

insights.claim: TSV prices come from formulaic AMM supply and demand within each venue, relying on arbitrageurs to keep them aligned; US equities move to 23/5 trading on December 6, improving reference prices, but weekend pricing depends on perpetual futures and is weaker.
insights.speaker: Brett Redford (Securitize)
insights.so_what: Expect weekend price dislocations in tokenized stocks - arbitrage opportunity and investor risk.
insights.quote: initially I think the weekends are you know people people need to be pretty careful

insights.claim: Robinhood's tokenized Hims & Hers offshore traded at $132 versus a Friday close just under $29 after a memecoin pool was paired with it.
insights.speaker: Laura Shin (host)
insights.so_what: Shows extreme AMM price-dislocation risk in permissionless tokenized stocks.

insights.claim: Redford warns offshore synthetic stock tokens carry counterparty risk - if the token issuer fails, holders could be wiped out - and permissionless trading risks OFAC breaches and untracked insider holdings.
insights.speaker: Brett Redford (Securitize)
insights.so_what: A synthetic-token issuer failure could reprice the whole offshore market and favor rights-bearing onshore tokens.
insights.quote: They could they could be completely wiped out in those positions.

insights.claim: Investor Will Manidis argued the market will trend to synthetic exposure because holding the underlying equity is unimportant or undesirable for marginal buyers, a view Redford rejects.
insights.speaker: Laura Shin (host)
insights.so_what: Key debate: whether rights-stripped synthetic exposure or full-rights tokens win share.
insights.quote: the market will trend towards synthetic exposure

insights.claim: ETFs are prominent among offshore synthetic activity and eligible for TSVs as NMS securities with issuer-sponsor consent; Securitize hopes to bring tokenized ETFs to market very soon.
insights.speaker: Jamie Selway; Brett Redford
insights.so_what: ETF issuers are likely early tokenization adopters.
